msg_type.description: TEMPORARY STOPGAP (BOT-301): explicit ROS message type (e.g. 'nav_msgs/msg/OccupancyGrid') for an inbound LiveKit data track. LiveKit DataTracks do not yet carry ROS type metadata, so a pure consumer cannot infer the type of a track it only receives (nothing on its local ROS graph publishes it). Set this on 'in'/'bidirectional' topics so the bridge can create the republishing publisher. Remove once DataTracks propagate the ROS type.

preserve_id.description: Inbound topics only. When true, the publishing participant's (sanitized) identity is prepended to the republished ROS topic name, e.g. /tf from participant robot-1 becomes /robot_1/tf. Prevents topic-name collisions when multiple participants publish the same topic. Ignored for outbound topics.

max_rate_hz.description: Outbound topics only. Optional cap (in Hz) on the rate at which this topic is forwarded to LiveKit, keeping unnecessary traffic off constrained links (e.g. throttle a high-rate /tf to render rate for a remote viewer). The bridge caches the most recent sample and a timer resends it at this rate (zero-order hold), so the configured rate is produced exactly regardless of the input rate; an idle topic is not re-sent. This is lossy for topics whose messages each carry distinct content (e.g. /tf aggregates transforms from multiple broadcasters) and adds up to one period of latency; it is ideal for large whole-state messages where only the newest value matters. Matched by literal topic name, not regex. Ignored for inbound topics.
